# ACNE

Acne is an inflammatory skin condition caused by excess sebum production, gland obstruction and infection with Cutibacterum acnes. Early disease manifests with black heads and white heads and little inflammation. Small papules and pustules are present in mild disease. Severe disease occurs when comedones, papules, pustules and less often cysts are present.

The goal of treatment is prevention and reeducation of new comedones and creating an environment that is inhibitory for C. acnes. General skin care treatment measures include utilizing gentle skin cleansers, avoiding aggressive scrubbing, using non-comedogenic skin products, and avoiding picking of lesions.

Diet's role in therapy remains uncertain.

Non-Antimicrobial therapy includes benzoyl peroxide topical/wash, salicylic acid topical, and tretinoin topical. These agents can be used as monotherapy in early disease and in addition to antimicrobial treatment in mild to severe disease.

## Early Disease:

Clindamycin 1% lotion topically q12h ($) [M]
< OR >
Erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h ($) [DI]

## Mild Disease:

Erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h ($) [DI]
< OR >
Doxycycline 50 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks
< OR >
Minocycline 50 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks

## Severe Disease:

Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks <AND> erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h
< OR >
Minocycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 12 weeks <AND> erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h
